concepts.name: Static versus runtime typing
concepts.summary: Explain that TypeScript checks types at compile time and then erases them, so the emitted JavaScript contains no type information.

concepts.name: Primitive type annotations
concepts.summary: Recall and write annotations for string, number, boolean, null, undefined and arrays on variables and parameters.

concepts.name: Type inference
concepts.summary: Understand how the compiler infers types from initial values so that annotations are not needed everywhere.

concepts.name: Function parameter and return types
concepts.summary: Annotate function parameters and return values and understand the errors raised when calls do not match.

concepts.name: Object type literals
concepts.summary: Describe the shape of an object with property names and types, including optional properties.

concepts.name: Compiling with tsc
concepts.summary: Recall that tsc type-checks .ts files and emits .js files, and read basic compiler error messages.

concepts.name: The any type
concepts.summary: Understand that any switches off type checking for a value and why it undermines safety.

misconceptions.text: TypeScript types are checked while the program runs and protect against bad data at runtime.
Every variable must have an explicit type annotation.
Using any is a harmless way to make errors go away.

concepts.name: Interfaces and type aliases
concepts.summary: Define named object shapes with interface and type, and apply them to parameters and variables.

concepts.name: Union types
concepts.summary: Combine types with | to accept several possible values and handle each case.

concepts.name: Type narrowing
concepts.summary: Use typeof, instanceof, equality and truthiness checks to narrow a union to a specific type within a branch.

concepts.name: Literal types and enums
concepts.summary: Restrict values to specific constants using literal unions or enums and choose between them.

concepts.name: Typed arrays and tuples
concepts.summary: Type arrays and fixed-length tuples and apply them to function arguments and return values.

concepts.name: Optional and readonly properties
concepts.summary: Mark properties optional or readonly and handle possibly undefined values safely.

concepts.name: Typing classes
concepts.summary: Annotate class properties and methods, use public, private and readonly modifiers, and implement interfaces.

concepts.name: Strict null checking
concepts.summary: Handle null and undefined explicitly when strict null checks are enabled.

misconceptions.text: Interfaces and type aliases are completely interchangeable in every situation.
A union type value lets you use any member of any of its types without checks.
The private modifier makes a class member inaccessible at runtime.

concepts.name: Generic functions and constraints
concepts.summary: Write functions with type parameters and constrain them with extends so types flow from input to output.

concepts.name: Generic interfaces and classes
concepts.summary: Define reusable containers and APIs parameterised by type, with defaults where useful.

concepts.name: Discriminated unions
concepts.summary: Model variants with a shared literal tag and use it for exhaustive narrowing, including a never check.

concepts.name: keyof and indexed access
concepts.summary: Use keyof, typeof and T[K] to tie property names and value types together safely.

concepts.name: Built-in utility types
concepts.summary: Apply Partial, Required, Pick, Omit, Record and ReturnType to derive types from existing ones.

concepts.name: tsconfig compiler options
concepts.summary: Configure target, module, strict and include settings and analyse how each changes checking and output.

concepts.name: Unknown versus any
concepts.summary: Contrast unknown with any and narrow unknown values before use, such as parsed JSON.

concepts.name: Declaration files and modules
concepts.summary: Use .d.ts files and @types packages to type JavaScript libraries and organise code with typed imports and exports.

misconceptions.text: Type assertions with as convert values and make them safe at runtime.
Generics are only needed for collections like arrays.
Turning on strict mode changes the generated JavaScript.

concepts.name: Conditional types and infer
concepts.summary: Write types that branch on type relationships and extract parts of types with infer.

concepts.name: Mapped types
concepts.summary: Transform every property of a type with mapped types, modifiers and key remapping.

concepts.name: Template literal types
concepts.summary: Build string types from unions and patterns to model keys, routes and event names.

concepts.name: Distributive conditional behaviour
concepts.summary: Predict how conditional types distribute over unions and when to prevent it.

concepts.name: Structural typing and variance
concepts.summary: Evaluate assignability using structural rules, and reason about covariance and contravariance in function parameters.

concepts.name: Overloads and type predicates
concepts.summary: Choose between overloads, generics and custom guards to give call sites precise types.

concepts.name: Type-safe API design
concepts.summary: Judge and design function and library signatures that infer well and prevent invalid states.

concepts.name: Project references and build performance
concepts.summary: Structure multi-package repositories with project references and diagnose slow type checking.

misconceptions.text: TypeScript uses nominal typing, so two types with the same shape are incompatible unless one declares the other.
Conditional types always evaluate a union as a whole rather than per member.
More complex types always make code safer and better.

concepts.name: Type-level programming limits
concepts.summary: Evaluate when recursive and computed types are justified given depth limits, compile cost and readability.

concepts.name: Soundness trade-offs
concepts.summary: Assess where TypeScript is deliberately unsound, such as bivariance, array covariance and assertions, and mitigate the risks.

concepts.name: Runtime validation bridging
concepts.summary: Design boundaries that link runtime validation of external data with static types, using schemas and branded types.

concepts.name: Library typing and declaration authoring
concepts.summary: Create declaration files and public type surfaces for libraries, using merging and augmentation and keeping them compatible across releases.

concepts.name: Compiler API and tooling
concepts.summary: Build tools such as analysers or code generators on the compiler and language service APIs.

concepts.name: Migration strategy for codebases
concepts.summary: Plan staged migration of large JavaScript codebases using allowJs, checkJs and tightening strictness over time.

concepts.name: Type design standards and review
concepts.summary: Establish and critique team conventions for type design, strictness and lint rules that balance safety with productivity.

misconceptions.text: If the code compiles with no errors, it is guaranteed free of type-related runtime errors.
The most precise possible type is always the best design for a public API.
A JavaScript codebase must be fully converted in one pass to benefit from TypeScript.
